title: Parkfield earthquakes

data.source: Parkfield magnitude-6 earthquakes: Bakun and Lindh (1985) for 1857 to 1966, USGS ComCat for 2004

prediction: The six gaps are more even than a memoryless fault gives (CV below the 5th percentile, P1), and forecasting forward a first-passage density beats a memoryless density in total log-probability (P2).
baseline: A memoryless (Poisson) fault. The field's Brownian passage time model is the count idea already.
why: Only one of the two predictions held. The gaps are more even than a memoryless fault, but forecasting forward the first-passage density did not beat the memoryless one. Six gaps is very little, and the count idea here is the standard Brownian passage time model in other words.
